title: A lifted relation in a cyclic square-zero extension obstructs finite Tor dimension
statement: Let $q:R'\twoheadrightarrow R$ be a surjection of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with kernel $(f)$ satisfying $(f)^2=0$. Multiplication on $(f)$ makes it an $R$-module: $rf$ means multiplication by any lift of $r\in R$. Put $I=\{r\in R:rf=0\}$. For integers $n,m\geq0$, put $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and $P'=R'[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, with the coefficientwise map $q_P:P'\to P$. Let $h_1,\ldots,h_m,r_1,\ldots,r_m\in P$ satisfy $\sum_{j=1}^m r_jh_j=0$, and assume every coefficient of every $r_j$ lies in $I$. Put $S=P/(h_1,\ldots,h_m)$ and let $IS$ be the ideal generated by the image of $I$. Suppose there are lifts $h'_j,r'_j\in P'$ and $g'\in P'$ with $q_P(h'_j)=h_j$, $q_P(r'_j)=r_j$, and $\sum_{j=1}^m r'_jh'_j=g'f$, such that the image $\bar g$ of $q_P(g')$ in $S/IS$ is not nilpotent (that is, $\bar g^a\ne0$ for every integer $a\geq1$). Then $S$ has no finite Tor dimension over $R$: there is no integer $d\geq0$ for which $\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(S,N)=0$ for every $R$-module $N$ and every integer $i>d$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules].

source.place: Tag 09PU (lemma-not-finite-pd), statement and proof, lines 1537–1566; the scalar g is written using an explicit lift g′ in P′.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-tate-free-resolution] to the given quotient $P\twoheadrightarrow S$ over the Noetherian ring $R$. This gives an augmented free resolution $A\to S$ whose degree zero part is $P$, whose positive homology vanishes, and whose underlying graded divided-power algebra has finitely many variables in each degree.

Apply [lem-sfb-square-zero-dga-curvature] to $A$, $R'\twoheadrightarrow R$ and $f$. Write $B=A/IA$ and choose the lifted operator and its curvature map $\theta$. The given relation and its chosen lifts satisfy every hypothesis of [lem-sfb-lifted-relation-curvature-class]; in particular $H_1(A)=0$ by Step 1. Thus obtain a cycle $z\in B_2$ with $[\theta(z)]=\bar g\in H_0(B)=S/IS$.

Put $u=\theta(z)\in B_0$. By the differential identity in [def-sfb-divided-power-dga], $d\gamma_a(z)=dz\,\gamma_{a-1}(z)=0$ for $a\geq1$. The identities of [lem-sfb-square-zero-dga-curvature] give $\theta(u)=0$ (negative degrees vanish) and, by induction on $0\leq k\leq a$, $\theta^k(\gamma_a(z))=u^k\gamma_{a-k}(z)$: apply the ordinary Leibniz rule, $\theta(u)=0$, and the divided-power rule at each induction step. In particular $\theta^a(\gamma_a(z))=u^a$. If $\gamma_a(z)=dv$ were a boundary, commutation of $\theta$ and $d$ would give $u^a=d(\theta^a v)$, hence $\bar g^a=[u]^a=0$ in $H_0(B)$. This contradicts nonnilpotence. Therefore $H_{2a}(B)\ne0$ for every $a\geq1$.

The augmented complex of Step 1 is a free $R$-resolution of $S$. Tensoring its terms with $R/I$ gives $A_i\otimes_R R/I\cong A_i/IA_i=B_i$, by $a\otimes\bar r\mapsto ra\bmod IA_i$ with inverse $\bar a\mapsto a\otimes1$. Thus the resolution formula of [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules] identifies $H_i(B)$ with $\operatorname{Tor}^R_i(S,R/I)$. If a finite bound $d\geq0$ existed as in the statement, take $a=d+1$ and $N=R/I$; then $2a>d$ would force this nonzero group to vanish, a contradiction.

The item statement agrees with 09PU hypothesis by hypothesis: using the lift g' in P' is the same as the source's g in (R/I)[x], since g'f only depends on g' modulo Ann(f) = q^-1(I). Step 1 (Tate resolution) gives A_0 = P, the resolution property, finitely many variables per degree and R-free terms. Step 2 meets every hypothesis of the lifted-relation node: H_1 = 0 comes from Step 1, and H_0(B) = S/IS by right exactness. Step 3 is correct: the induction for theta^k(gamma_a(z)), theta(u) = 0 in degree -2, and theta commuting with d are verified. Its replacement of the source's xi^n by gamma_n(xi) is a correct fix of a source error (in F_p<T>, T^p = 0). Step 4 identifies A tensor R/I with B, so Tor_2a(S, R/I) = H_2a(B) is nonzero. I checked the new nodes as follows. The DP-DGA definition matches 09PG axioms (1)-(7) and 09PJ. The curvature node checks out: D^2 lands in fA' and kills q^-1(I)A'; iota is bijective because A' is free over R' and Ann_R'(f) = q^-1(I); and the unsigned Leibniz rule, theta d = d theta and the divided-power rule all hold, using (Dx)^2 = 0. The lifted-relation node, re-derived for an arbitrary lift and augmented A, gives theta(z) = phi'(g') + Dc with the middle term killed by f, and the m = 0 case holds. The Tate node holds for S = 0 and S = P. Searches of the DAG, live and side-live, and the blueprint (Tate, divided power, square zero, Tor dimension, Gulliksen, 09PG-09PU) find no duplicate; the 09PQ Koszul/self-Tor nodes state something different. lean.statement: theorem square_zero_relation_not_finite_tor_dimension {R : Type u} {R' : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing R'] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R'] (q : R' →+* R) (hq : Function.Surjective q) (f : R') (hker : RingHom.ker q = Ideal.span {f}) (hsq : (Ideal.span {f} : Ideal R') ^ 2 = ⊥) (I : Ideal R) (hI : I = Ideal.map q (Ideal.span {f}).annihilator) (n m : ℕ) (h r : Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R) (hrel : ∑ j, r j * h j = 0) (hcoeff : ∀ (j : Fin m) (d : Fin n →₀ ℕ), (r j).coeff d ∈ I) (J : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)) (hJ : J = Ideal.span (Set.range h)) (h' r' : Fin m → MvPolynomial (Fin n) R') (g' : MvPolynomial (Fin n) R') (hlift : ∀ j : Fin m, MvPolynomial.map q (h' j) = h j) (rlift : ∀ j : Fin m, MvPolynomial.map q (r' j) = r j) (hrel' : ∑ j, r' j * h' j = g' * MvPolynomial.C f) (hg : ¬ IsNilpotent (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.map ((Ideal.Quotient.mk J).comp MvPolynomial.C) I) (Ideal.Quotient.mk J (MvPolynomial.map q g')))) : ¬ ∃ d : ℕ, ∀ (N : ModuleCat.{u} R) (i : ℕ), d < i → IsZero (((Tor' (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj (ModuleCat.of R (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R ⧸ J))).obj N)

reviewed_lean.note: Every clause matches Stacks 09PU and the node: Noetherian R and R' (universes u, v), surjective q, ker = (f) with (f)^2 = 0, I pinned to map q Ann(span f) (equal to {r : rf = 0} since f^2 = 0), all coefficients in I, J = span(range h), lifts with sum r'h' = g'·C f, non-nilpotence in S/IS via map (mk J ∘ C) I, conclusion ¬∃d over Tor' with S in the first variable and ModuleCat.{u} test modules (R/I is u-small). Edge cases n=0, m=0, f=0, J=⊤, d=0 are consistent.
